title: Typhoon Champi causes NT$270 million in agricultural losses in Taiwan

 Yunlin County accounts for 53% of damage, with garlic suffering the heaviest losses
   Oct. 27, 2026 15:23
 Flooded greenhouse and damaged crops following Typhoon Champi. (Cabinet photo)
 1468 TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Typhoon Champi caused an estimated NT$269.9 million (US$8.5 million) in agricultural losses in Taiwan, with Yunlin County accounting for more than half of the total, the Ministry of Agriculture said.
 The ministry's Department of Statistics said it compiled the damage assessment from local governments and agricultural agencies as of 11 a.m. Tuesday. The damage included NT$247.91 million in crop losses and NT$21.9 million in damage to private facilities.
 Yunlin County suffered the heaviest losses at NT$143.27 million, or 53% of the total. Taichung followed with NT$42.13 million, Miaoli County with NT$25.46 million, New Taipei with NT$16.29 million, and Hualien County with NT$11.13 million.
 Garlic was the most severely affected crop, with estimated losses of NT$63.59 million. The storm damaged 451 hectares of garlic fields, equivalent to total crop failure across 151 hectares.
 Peanuts were the second-most affected crop, with losses of NT$19.56 million across 678 hectares of damaged fields. Other major losses included NT$12.36 million for pears, NT$11.65 million for onions, and NT$11.53 million for ponkan mandarins.
 Overall, the storm affected 4,804 hectares of farmland, with damage averaging 21% across affected crops. The losses were equivalent to total crop failure across 1,031 hectares.
 Livestock losses were estimated at about NT$90,000, mainly involving pigs. Damage to private facilities totaled NT$21.9 million, including NT$2.48 million in agricultural infrastructure, NT$8.57 million in livestock and poultry facilities, and NT$10.85 million in fishing infrastructure.
